title: One debrief and one death path
overseerSummary: Lands first in wave 2. Missions.debrief becomes the single per-survivor hook that wounds, the ledger and the service record plug into. Death order fixed: snapshot bonds, Roster.fall, Bonds.mourn, Crew.mourn.

proposals.title: One mission debrief for the Gate and the Field, and one death path
proposals.problem: Contracts on the Field tab end through Sortie.settle, which skips four hooks that zone runs on the Gate tab get from Missions.finish. Checked by running real contracts headless (game.html's 61 scripts under a stub DOM, Sortie.launch then Sortie.skip, three contracts in a row with one mage/cleric/fighter squad): class XP stays 0.00 on every member, stamina stays full, the mage's mana is 108/108 after the contract; only morale changes (55, 35, 20 across the three, from -12 per loss and -6 per death). The class loot multiplier (x1.1 to x1.35 on eight classes, printed in the class text) pays nothing on a contract, Classes.fought has no caller, and condition.js's stated purpose (rest before a mission matters) does not apply to the main mission format. Deaths enter by three routes and only the Field route grieves: Gate deaths call Crew.mourn only, an altar sacrifice calls neither, and Bonds.tidy has no callers. Gate runs forge no bonds.
evidence: missions.js:256 Classes.returned (class XP) for survivors; missions.js:259-260 Condition.spend and Condition.outcome; missions.js:271 Classes.partyLoot. None appear in sortie.js settle (439-541), which calls Condition.outcome at 517 and Crew.completed/Crew.mourn at 511-512.

sortie.js:479 `worth = Math.round((25 + m.level * 30) * m.reward * sideMult * (1 + over) * (escaped ? 0.35 : 1))`: no loot term. classes.js loot: lines 422, 583, 613, 628, 692, 708, 735, 863 (alchemist 1.1, trapper 1.1, scout 1.05, rogue 1.1, thief 1.35, spy 1.15, saboteur 1.1, beguiler 1.1).

classes.js:1579-1581 trained, fought, returned; grep: `fought` has no caller, `returned` only missions.js:256. classes.js:60 XP = { trainTick 0.03, encounter 0.15, mission 1.5 }; RANKS at 8/24/60/140 (classes.js:50-56).

condition.js:24-27 'Nothing here reaches into a fight' against combat.js:76-88 reading staminaFrac and poolFrac at fighter build; condition.js spend() takes casts x max(4, 6% of the pool) from the caster pool.

Deaths: roster.js:87 fall(); callers sortie.js:450, missions.js:265, sacrifice.js:181. Only sortie.js:464 -> game.js:380 grieve -> Bonds.mourn. game.js:493 (Gate deaths) calls Crew.mourn only; game.js:828-838 sacrificeTo and game.js:824 release call neither; bonds.js:251 tidy has no callers; roster.js:91 returns early for an existing record, so listeners placed after it fire once.

Scratch pools.js, 210 combat-backed sorties, 694 survivors (every one has a mana or spirit pool): casts per survivor p25/p50/p90 = 2/5/14; Condition.spend() would remove 12%/30%/60% of the cond pool at p25/p50/p75 and 8% of survivors would be drained to zero; mean share by class: alchemist 0.57, cleric 0.50, mage 0.45, ranger 0.42, rogue 0.38, fighter 0.31, barbarian 0.23. The fighter's own end-of-run pool is already refilled by sortie.js REGEN (mana 0.96-1.00), so casts, not the end pool, are the cost to carry home.

Mean sortie length 346 in-game seconds = 69 real seconds = 6.9 town ticks (1,800 runs; missiontypes.js:46 stepMs 200, game.js:8 TICK_MS 10000). The flat Gate stamina cost 25 + 1.5 x level is 34 at level 6; rest returns 4 + 0.2 x CON per tick (condition.js REST_BASE, REST_PER_CON), about 5 ticks to recover.
Scratch lootshare.js, 78 won sorties: mean contract worth 251 gems, mean kill-drop gems 75, so drops are 23% of gem income.
proposals.change: 1) missions.js: add Missions.debrief(state, { survivors: [{ c, hp, casts }], fallen, won, level, fights }) returning { lootMult, lines }. Per survivor: Classes.returned(c, { won }) plus Classes.fought(c, min(fights, 3)) (the cap is a Gate run's three encounters, so a contract and a Gate run pay at most 1.5 + 0.45 class XP); Condition.spend(c, { staminaCost: 25 + 1.5 x level, casts }) (the existing Gate formula for both formats); Condition.outcome(c, { won, lost: fallen }); when Bonds is loaded, Bonds.together(survivors, 'mission', 1, runs) with runs 1 for a win and 0.5 for a loss, then 'won' and 'survived' as sortie.js:459-462 does now. lootMult = Classes.partyLoot(survivors). Modules are reached through typeof-guarded accessors like the existing CL() and CO(), because missions.js also loads in field.html and Node. 2) Missions.finish builds its survivors from run.members (hp = members[id].hp, casts = members[id].casts, fights = run.encounter) and Sortie.settle builds them from the squad actors (fighter.hp / maxHp, fighter.stats.casts, run.fights, a counter resolve() increments and persist() stores). The inline calls at missions.js:256, 259-260, 271 and sortie.js:455-463, 511-517 are removed. Casts are saved in the actor's combat record (field.js saveActor / sortie.js fighterFor restore) so a reload does not reset them. 3) Loot: Sortie.settle multiplies the amount of each gems and resource drop in run.loot by lootMult; the contract fee `worth` is not multiplied. The settle line prints 'drops x1.35 (Thief)'. The Gate keeps partyLoot x mission.reward. 4) One death path: Roster.fall stays the only function that removes a body from the roster. After it writes the record it calls listeners registered with Roster.onFall(fn). game.js registers one that runs grieve(record) (game.js:380), Crew.mourn(state, logLine) and Bonds.tidy. The G().grieve call (sortie.js:464) and the Crew.mourn calls (sortie.js:512, game.js:493) are removed. Sacrifice.apply already calls Roster.fall (sacrifice.js:181) and so grieves; release() (game.js:824) is not a death and calls Bonds.tidy only. Inside fall() the record is built before the listeners run, so a proposal that copies bonds into the record can do it first. 5) sortie.js party card helper partyFacts(c): stamina band and caster pool percent (Condition.describe) and 'ready in N ticks, limited by X' from Condition.readyIn(c, restMult, fed) = max of wound ticks / recovery rate, (RESTED - poolFrac) / (POOL_REGEN x restMult), and (RESTED x max - stamina) / rest per tick. Wounds, meals, will-axis, cohesion and loop-readout add their lines to this one helper. 6) condition.js header (lines 24-27) is corrected to say combat.js reads stamina and pool at fighter build.
proposals.playerEffect: A contract costs the squad what a zone run costs. Casters leave the sortie with a smaller pool: the median survivor loses 30% of it and 8% lose all of it; refilling to 85% takes about 8 resting ticks from a 30% loss, 23 from 60%, 43 from empty (POOL_REGEN 2% per tick at rest x1.0). The 34-point stamina cost is back in about 5 ticks, so the pool is the binding clock for casters and wounds (systems-wounds-via-injured) for the hurt. These do not add: the picker shows the largest and names it, so the kitchen, bed quality and a second squad become part of running contracts. Class XP and specialisation progress from contract work, including for a character on a star trial. A Thief party adds about 8% to a contract's gems (x1.35 on the 23% that are drops) and the log says so. Sacrificing the bonded partner of a friend costs the friend morale, as a battlefield death does.
proposals.secondOrder: Condition's party-picker inputs become decisions. Class specialise() can fire from contract work. Gate runs gain bond formation and grief, so Gate work now builds pair runs that systems-cohesion-from-pairs reads on the Field. Spent stamina feeds the resolve seed in systems-will-axis (isSpent), so sending a squad out twice without rest makes it leave fights earlier. Offline catch-up (MAX_OFFLINE_TICKS 2880) refills every pool, so the cost bites in active play only. Quests.pass is unchanged. The Roster.onFall hook is the place for loop-record to snapshot bonds and for any later death consequence.
proposals.risks: Class XP is at most 1.95 per run in both formats, but contracts can be launched more often than Gate runs; the headless harness should report XP per real hour before the cap is accepted. Roster listeners run inside Missions.tick when a Gate run finishes, so grief log lines appear mid-tick; field.html and Node register no listener and behave as today. Gate end HP includes the quarter-HP rest after the last fight (missions.js:196), so Gate runs produce fewer wounds than contracts; left as is. Loot applies to drops only, so a Thief party gains about 8% on gems, not 35%; if the class text promising x1.35 is read as a pay multiplier, the contract fee would need the term too, which measured-wise is a 35% raise on the main income source and is not proposed. sortie.js and missions.js are also edited by wounds, cohesion, meals and will-axis; this lands first in this lens.
proposals.response: Design attack, class XP: returned() is unchanged at 1.5 and fought() is capped at the Gate's three encounters, so one contract is worth at most one Gate run (1.95 XP); the stamina term uses the Gate's flat formula (34 at level 6, about 5 ticks to recover), not a clock-based figure, and I agree it is noise by itself; mana is the real limiter and is the measured table above, not 'empty after one contract' (median 30% of the pool, 8% emptied). Loot: applied to drops only and printed in the settle line; this is a 23% slice of gem income, measured on 78 sorties, not a pay rise on the main income. Death path: one entry, Roster.fall plus listeners, and it is the only browser caller of grief. Gate bonds and grief: kept because the pair ledger feeds cohesion, which the antagonist assigned to systems-cohesion-from-pairs; Gate cohesion itself is not added. Engineering attack: the death path no longer sits in game.js alone, since Missions.finish keeps calling Roster.fall and the listener fires inside it; missions.js stays loadable without Bonds or Crew through guarded accessors; debrief lands first and hosts wounds, record and arcs; the loot multiplier is printed and the contract card figure should read 'before class loot' (cleanup-contract-honesty); the combined downtime budget is stated in ticks above and shown as one 'ready in' figure. Cast counts after a reload were an additional gap I found (fighters are rebuilt on resume), handled in step 2.

verdicts.attack: Class XP per contract at XP.mission 1.5 flat (classes.js:60, 1581) with several contracts an hour outruns the rank tuning; the Thief's x1.35 on contracts is a straight pay rise on the main income source; the stamina term (about 68) recovers in 11 ticks so it is noise, and the mana term is a second rate limiter on casters on top of loop-wounds. Gate runs gaining bonds and grief changes a mode nobody asked about.
verdicts.evidenceCheck: Verified: missions.js:256 Classes.returned, 258-260 Condition.spend/outcome, 265 Roster.fall, 271 partyLoot; sortie.js settle() (439-541) calls only Condition.outcome at 517; worth at sortie.js:479 has no loot term; classes.js:1579-1581 and grep: fought() has no caller; combat.js:83-88 reads the pools; game.js:493 Gate deaths call Crew.mourn only; sacrifice.js:181 and game.js:828-838 call neither grieve nor Bonds.mourn; Bonds.tidy (bonds.js:251) has no caller; MT.TIME.stepMs 200 at missiontypes.js:43-47.
verdicts.demand: It is the hook every settle-touching proposal plugs into, so it lands first with one owner for sortie.js settle() and missions.js finish(). Class XP scaled by encounters through Classes.fought with returned() reduced so a contract is worth about one Gate run. The loot multiplier applied to the resource payout or capped at x1.15 on contracts until measured. The single death entry in game.js becomes the only browser caller of Roster.fall. Gate cohesion stays with systems-cohesion-from-pairs.

verdicts.attack: Three changes in one: a shared debrief, Gate bond/grief wiring, and a single death path. The death path cannot sit in game.js as written: Missions.finish calls Roster.fall itself (missions.js:265) before game.js settleMission runs, and missions.js also runs in field.html and Node without Bonds or Crew. Caster pools: fighter.stats.casts accumulates across every skirmish of a sortie because fighters persist (sortie.js:120-152), and spend() takes 6% of the pool per cast (condition.js:188), so every caster comes home empty after one contract and needs about 50 resting ticks; with loop-wounds and stamina that is three downtime clocks on one roster with no stated budget. Gate runs gaining bonds and grief is a balance change nobody asked for.
verdicts.evidenceCheck: Verified missions.js:256 (Classes.returned), 259-260 (Condition.spend/outcome), 271 (partyLoot); settle() calls only Condition.outcome (sortie.js:517); classes.js:1579-1581, and grep: fought has no caller, returned only at missions.js:256, partyLoot only at missions.js:271; bonds.js:251 tidy has no caller; game.js:493 Crew.mourn only for Gate deaths; sacrificeTo (game.js:828-838) grieves nothing; MT.TYPES.extermination.duration(6) = 1140 in-game s = 228 real s = about 23 ticks (TICK_MS 10000, TIME.scale 5); RANKS at 8/24/60/140 so XP.mission 1.5 is about five contracts to Adept.
verdicts.demand: 1) Missions.debrief lands first and hosts every per-survivor hook (wounds, record, arcs call into it). 2) Specify the death path: either Roster.fall becomes the single entry with optional after-hooks, or the fall moves out of missions.js into game.settleMission; coordinate the bond snapshot with loop-record. 3) Print the loot multiplier on the settle line and mark the contract card figure 'before class loot' so cleanup-contract-honesty's number stays traceable. 4) A combined downtime budget with loop-wounds, stated in ticks.
